candidates.change_summary: Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the state variable is never updated.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the variable stores the block number instead of the timestamp.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = 0;` so the variable is reset instead of set to the current timestamp.
Invert the time guard to `require(block.timestamp < pastBlockTime);` so subsequent calls revert and `pastBlockTime` is never updated after the first state in which it holds a nonzero value.
Delete the statement that updates pastBlockTime to the current timestamp.
Assign the current block number instead of the current timestamp to pastBlockTime.
Assign a constant value instead of the current timestamp to pastBlockTime.
Delete the statement 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' so pastBlockTime is never updated after a successful call.
Replace 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' with 'pastBlockTime = block.number;' so a different value is stored.
Replace 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' with 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;' so an off-by-one value is stored.
Move 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' inside the if-branch so pastBlockTime is only updated when the payout branch executes.
Delete the statement that updates pastBlockTime, so it stays 0 forever and calls never get blocked by the timestamp check.
Replace the pastBlockTime update with block.number instead of block.timestamp, changing the observable public value and the re-entry guard semantics.
Invert the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 != 0, changing when the payout occurs.
Delete the require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) check, allowing multiple calls within the same timestamp.
Relax the timestamp check from strictly greater to greater-or-equal, allowing a second call in the same timestamp.
Delete the assignment `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the stored timestamp is never updated.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so a different value is stored.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored value is incremented beyond the current timestamp.
Insert `pastBlockTime = 0;` at the start of the function so any successful call resets the stored value to zero.
